textbookText: 11.5 Specific Heat Capacity and Change in Temperature Suppose an equal amount of heat is given to two different substances of equal mass m but of different specific heat capacities. Let s1 and s2 are respective specific heat capacities. Similarly , let 1 and 2 be respective changes in temperature. Then, from the given condition, Heat given to first system = Heat given to second system s1m1 = s2m2 or, s11 = s22 or, s1 = 2 s2 1 i.e., 1 s This indicates that the change in the temperature of a substance is inversely proportional to its specific heat capacity for constant heat supplied or absorbed. 11.6 Applications of High and Low Specific Heat Capacity A substance which has value of specific heat capacity can absorb large amount of heat from any object brought in thermal contact. As a result of this, temperature of object in contact reduces by sufficiently large value but its own temperature changes almost negligibly. This property of substance can be used as cooling agent. Water has high specific heat capacity and shows such behavior. Therefore, water can be used, (i) as cooling agent in many heating appliances and in running vehicles (ii) to lower down temperature of a person suffering from high fever.

Also, a substance which has high value of specific heat capacity can release large amount of heat to anybody brought in thermal contact. As a result of this, temperature of object in contact increases by sufficiently large value but its own temperature changes almost negligibly. This property of substance can be used as heating agent. Water has high specific heat capacity and shows such behavior. Therefore, water can be used (i) as heating agent in room heating system (ii) as heating agent in hot water bag Physics, Grade 11 | 249

Substance which has low value of specific heat capacity can absorb or lose almost negligible amount of heat from or to any other body brought in thermal contact and immediately it attains thermal equilibrium. This action does not bring any change in thermal configuration of the body in contact. Mercury has such property. Therefore, mercury can be used as thermometric substance.
Similarly copper also has low value of specific heat capacity so that it can be used as material of calorimeter.

Also, substance which has low value of specific heat capacity suffers sufficiently large change in temperature even from the small amount of heat applied. Cooking oil has such property. Therefore, cooking oil can be used to make fried food items (easier and faster cooking).
Similarly massage oil has low specific heat capacity so that it gets heated sufficiently from the heat of friction during massage.
